Schedule

CSS 555 · Evaluating Software Design · Winter 2027draft

Winter 2027 · Days, time, and room: TBD (planned as Monday/Wednesday, 2-hour sessions)

The course spine is predict, then measure. Each quality dimension from the catalog (performance, scalability, maintainability, usability, security) gets an analytical evaluation (prescriptive: models, structure, and reviews of the design) and an empirical evaluation (agile: measurements of the running system or its history). Students record a prediction before measuring, then explain the gap. Design is evaluated at every level (architecture, modules and interfaces, code structure), with the implementation as evidence; bugs enter only as defect data about the design.

Quarter Dates

  • Instruction: Mon Jan 4 – Fri Mar 12, 2027
  • Holidays (no class): Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Mon Jan 18; Presidents' Day, Mon Feb 15
  • Finals week: Mar 15–19, 2027

The two Monday holidays leave 18 sessions.

What "good design" means at each level (architecture, module and interface, code); evaluation as evidence; ISO/IEC 25010 quality model; prescriptive vs. agile evaluation. ICA: rank two designs, then list the evidence that would change your ranking M what measurement is and why do it; CT Evaluation as Evidence

ICA: rewrite vague requirements as scenarios and SLOs M goal-based framework; CT Quality-Attribute Scenarios and Utility Trees; CT Service Levels; SRE Ch. 4 (Service Level Objectives); B Ch. 3 (optional) Paper sign-up
S3 2 Jan 11 M Architecture reviews: ATAM (utility trees; risks, non-risks, sensitivity points, tradeoff points), lighter variants (ARID, TARA, checklists, ADR and pull-request design reviews); what 15 years of ATAM data show. ICA: mini-ARID on a real design document CT Scenario-Based Evaluation; Bellomo, Gorton & Kazman (2015); Woods (2011); B Ch. 21 (optional)
S4 2 Jan 13 W Measurement as evidence: measurement scales and what each permits, internal vs. external attributes, construct and internal validity, variance and repetition, comparing two measurements (confidence intervals, effect size). ICA: write the measurement plan for one E0 scenario M basics of measurement, empirical investigation, and analyzing measurement data; CT Evaluation as Evidence (measurement sections); Kitchenham, Pfleeger & Fenton (1995) E0 (Sun Jan 17)
3 Jan 18 M Martin Luther King Jr. Day: no class
Part II: Performance, Scalability, Resilience
S5 3 Jan 20 W Performance, predict: latency vs. throughput, tail latency, Little's Law, utilization law, queueing intuition, back-of-envelope estimation. ICA: predict the reference app's latency at twice the load CT Predicting Performance; Dean & Barroso (2013)
S6 4 Jan 25 M Performance, measure: benchmarking method, load generation (k6 or Locust), profiling, USE and RED methods, OpenTelemetry tracing. Lab 1: load-test the reference app; compare with the S5 prediction CT Measuring Performance; SRE Ch. 6 (Monitoring Distributed Systems)
S7 4 Jan 27 W Scalability: Amdahl's law, Universal Scalability Law, scale cube, data partitioning. Lab 2: fit the USL to measured throughput CT Scalability Models; Amdahl (1967)
S8 5 Feb 1 M Resilience: stress and soak tests, failure-mode analysis, chaos experiments, SLO-based evaluation. Lab 3: fault injection on the reference app CT Resilience Experiments; Basiri et al. (2016)
Part III: Maintainability and Usability
S9 5 Feb 3 W Maintainability, predict: module and class design (deep vs. shallow modules, information hiding, design smells); coupling and cohesion, CK metrics, instability and abstractness; dependency structure matrices and cycles at module and service level M structure metrics; CT Maintainability from Structure; Parnas (1972); O, KH (optional) E1 (Sun Feb 7)
S10 6 Feb 8 M Maintainability, measure: change coupling, hotspots, defect clustering (bug-fix commits by module), architectural debt, debt prioritization; why single-number quality scores mislead. Lab 4: mine the project system's git history T hotspots and change-coupling chapters; CT Maintainability from History; Xiao et al. (2016); B Ch. 23 (optional)
S11 6 Feb 10 W Usability, predict: heuristic evaluation, cognitive walkthrough, keystroke-level model; API and developer-experience usability CT Inspection Methods and Predictive Models (CSS 478 chapters); Nielsen & Molich (1990); Myers & Stylos (2016)
7 Feb 15 M Presidents' Day: no class
S12 7 Feb 17 W Usability, measure: think-aloud testing, task success and time, System Usability Scale (SUS); how many users are enough. ICA: run a 3-user pilot in class CT Usability Testing (CSS 478 chapter); Nielsen & Landauer (1993) E2 (Sun Feb 21)
Part IV: Security and Continuous Evaluation
S13 8 Feb 22 M Security, predict: design principles, data-flow diagrams, STRIDE, attack trees. ICA: threat-model the reference app CT Threat Modeling; Saltzer & Schroeder (1975)

S16 9 Mar 3 W Tradeoffs and reporting: CBAM, risk themes, writing findings for decision makers; validity threats in reported evidence and Goodhart's law M metrics for decision support; CT Tradeoffs and Reporting; Kazman, Asundi & Klein (2001) E3 (Sun Mar 7)

Project Milestones

Teams of 3–4 evaluate one open-source system all quarter. Labs run on a shared reference app (TeaStore) so lab grading is comparable; milestones apply the same methods to the team's system. The CSS 553 Spring 2026 system (the UWB social network) is a pre-approved house system; with the team's permission, a house-system E4 report becomes the evaluation CSS 553 teams inherit in Spring 2027.

Milestone Deliverable Due Points
E0 Evaluation plan: system choice and approval, utility tree with 10–15 measurable scenarios across all five dimensions, method and measurement plan (Goal-Question-Metric) per scenario Sun Jan 17 15
E1 Performance, scalability, resilience: predictions, load and fault tests, USL fit, prediction-vs-measurement gap analysis Sun Feb 7 45
E2 Maintainability: module- and architecture-level structural metrics, design smells, hotspot, defect, and architectural-debt analysis, top debt items Sun Feb 21 35
E3 Usability and security: heuristic evaluation, 5-user test with SUS, threat model, ASVS Level 1 check, scan results Sun Mar 7 45
E4 Final report in ATAM form (risks, non-risks, sensitivity and tradeoff points, risk themes), fitness functions and conformance checks committed to the system's CI, presentation Presentations Mar 8 and 10; report Sun Mar 14 60
Total 200
